info.syllabusName: Tourism destinations and routes of Vietnam_Tuyến điểm du lịch Việt Nam
info.syllabusEnglish: Tourism destinations and routes of Vietnam
info.timeAllocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
info.description:
Description: The module equips students with knowledge about tourist destinations within Vietnam such as geographical distribution, social, economic, cultural, and tourism development of leading source 7 tourism regions. From a geographical point of view, based on the classification of tourism resources, the countries of origin of tourists, or generating areas; and the routes traveled between these two sets of locations teaches students how to design, develop and evaluate a tour itinerary.

Effectively apply AI to the course.

Objectives

This course helps students to master the characteristics of regions and the connections between them, from which students apply this knowledge to design appropriate travel itineraries and to present them in a convincing, attractive way to tourists/customers.

Teaching Method:

The course is designed based on the blended learning method. Students are required to read slides before coming to class. In class, the lecturer recalls the lesson and organizes discussion activities.

The course includes a lot of practical sessions for interpreting and building travel itineraries.

<- Students must attend more than 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Promptly access to http://flm.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information>

assessments.noQuestion: Each student shoud answer and contribute ideas in lecture time at least 3 times during the course. Questions will be given by lecturer depending on each lecture.
assessments.knowledgeSkill: Skill to defense and support ideas, Show your own knowledge about destinations and social issues
assessments.gradingGuide: Participation grade will be given based on students' preparation, and quantity as well as quality of participation in classroom; quality of participation is demonstrated through asking relevant questions, making statements that add to and facilitate class discussion, and builds upon others’ comments. Class preparation and pre-reading before lecture will be assessed upon individuals' understanding and ability to answer questions in the class. Individuals will be called up randomly to be assessed.
assessments.note: Consideration of the student attendance and participation
